issues.user_problem: Users are interrupted before understanding the site
signals_to_detect: Modal or overlay element appears on page load (no user interaction required)
Popup blocks main content with no visible dismiss button or skip option
Newsletter signup or permission request modal appears immediately on homepage
Modal or fullscreen layer appears before user can interact with product content
issues.recommendation: Delay permission pop-ups until user intent is clear
acceptance_criteria: No pop-ups appear before first meaningful interaction
negative_signals: Pop-ups appear only after user has scrolled 50%+ of page or spent 30+ seconds
Modals include clear X button or 'No thanks' option in visible corner
User can click outside modal to dismiss it
Pop-up appears only on exit intent or after meaningful interaction
issues.context_notes: Only flag pop-ups that appear within first 5 seconds or before user interacts. Do not flag: Exit-intent modals, scroll-triggered (>50% page), or time-delayed (30s+). Industry context: Legal compliance pop-ups (cookies) may appear immediately; flag intrusive marketing/newsletter pop-ups.

issues.user_problem: Users struggle to change language/location
signals_to_detect: Language or location selector hidden in footer or buried in menu
No language/location toggle visible in header or navigation
Language selector present but not easily identifiable (generic icon or text label)
Multi-region ecommerce site without visible language switching option
issues.recommendation: Move language selector to header with clear icon
acceptance_criteria: Language selector visible on all pages in header
negative_signals: Language/country selector visible in header without scrolling
Flag icon or language name clearly displayed in top navigation
Current language/country shown with dropdown arrow indicator
Selector accessible within one click from any page
issues.context_notes: Only flag if language selector genuinely hard to find (requires >2 clicks or hidden). Do not flag: Footer placement if clearly visible, or flag/language name in header. Industry context: Single-market sites may not need prominent language selector.

issues.user_problem: Too many CTAs overwhelm users
signals_to_detect: Multiple competing CTAs for the SAME user action (e.g., 3+ variations of 'Buy Now' or 'Add to Cart')
Primary CTA not visually distinguished from secondary CTAs (same size, color, prominence)
Homepage hero section contains 3+ CTAs with equal visual weight competing for immediate action
Multiple checkout CTAs visible simultaneously (e.g., 'Checkout', 'Express Checkout', 'Quick Buy' all equally prominent)
issues.recommendation: Reduce CTAs and establish hierarchy
acceptance_criteria: One primary CTA visually dominant
negative_signals: Service category buttons with clear color-coding for different features (e.g., 'Used Products' green, 'Rent Now' blue)
Navigation menu items are text links or minimal buttons, not primary action CTAs
Primary CTA uses solid color while secondary actions use outlined/ghost button style
CTAs lead to different features/services, not competing for same conversion action
issues.context_notes: Do not count: (1) Navigation category links, (2) Service feature buttons with clear differentiation, (3) Secondary utility links. Only flag when multiple CTAs compete for the SAME conversion action.

issues.user_problem: Users struggle to scan products
signals_to_detect: Product cards vary in layout, height, or content structure across listing
Add-to-cart button placed inconsistently (bottom for some, hover for others)
Product price, rating, or image placement differs between cards on same page
Some cards show additional info (SKU, tags) while others do not
issues.recommendation: Standardize card layout and CTA placement
acceptance_criteria: All cards follow same layout
negative_signals: All product cards show same information in same positions (image top, price bottom, title middle)
Rating stars appear in same location on all cards that have reviews
All cards use same image aspect ratio and size
Badges (sale, new, low stock) appear in consistent corner position
issues.context_notes: Variation in card content is acceptable if information hierarchy is consistent (e.g., always price at bottom, image at top). Only flag when: Critical info (price, title, image) appears in different locations across cards OR some cards missing essential data. Do not flag: Intentional variations for different product types (digital vs physical) or optional information (ratings only shown when reviews exist).

issues.user_problem: Users lack trust before purchase
signals_to_detect: No delivery timeframe visible anywhere on PDP (not near price, not in product details, not in any section)
Shipping cost only revealed at checkout, not shown anywhere on PDP
Return policy link completely absent from PDP (not in footer, not in product info, not anywhere visible)
No trust indicators (warranties, guarantees) visible anywhere in product area or details
issues.recommendation: Show shipping/returns near product title
acceptance_criteria: Policies visible without scrolling
negative_signals: Delivery timeframe displayed anywhere on PDP (near price, in details section, or clearly visible)
Shipping cost calculator or flat rate shown on PDP before add-to-cart
Return policy clearly linked or mentioned in product section (footer counts)
Trust badges (warranty, guarantee, returns) visible on PDP in any section
issues.context_notes: Only flag if 3+ policy items are COMPLETELY missing from PDP (not just suboptimally placed). Presence in footer, expandable sections, or anywhere visible on page counts as 'available'. Focus on complete absence of: (1) delivery time, (2) shipping cost info, (3) return policy, (4) warranties. If 2 or fewer missing, do not flag.

refinement_v3_4.sehaa_finding: Flagged when condition not fully met

issues.user_problem: Users don't know required steps
signals_to_detect: Mandatory selection steps (size, color, quantity) not clearly marked as required
Add-to-cart button disabled or grayed out without explanation until options selected
No visible instruction text explaining option selections before add-to-cart is available
Error messages appear only after attempting to add product without required selections
issues.recommendation: Guide users step-by-step before add to cart
acceptance_criteria: System guides user through selections
negative_signals: Required dropdowns marked with asterisk (*) or 'Required' label before interaction
Helpful text above dropdowns explains why selection is needed
Add-to-cart button clearly disabled with tooltip explaining what's needed
Default option shown for non-critical selections
issues.context_notes: Only flag if requirements are unclear AND user gets error. Do not flag: Visual indicators (disabled button, asterisks) even if not perfect. Industry context: Configurable products (tech, apparel) require option selection; flag unclear communication, not the requirement itself.

issues.user_problem: Users cannot continue shopping
signals_to_detect: Add-to-cart action immediately redirects to checkout without option to continue shopping
No Continue Shopping or Back to Products link visible after item added
Cart page forces checkout with no navigation back to product browsing
Shopping cart overlay or modal lacks return option to keep shopping
issues.recommendation: Use add-to-cart overlay with continue shopping
acceptance_criteria: Overlay allows continue shopping
negative_signals: 'Continue Shopping' button visible after add-to-cart action
Add-to-cart triggers mini-cart drawer that allows continuing or going to cart
User remains on PDP after adding item, with confirmation message
Cart page includes prominent 'Back to Shopping' or category links
issues.context_notes: Only flag if no way to continue shopping after add-to-cart. Do not flag: Brief redirect followed by continue option, or mini-cart that allows continuing. Industry context: Some niches (tickets, limited items) may intentionally push to checkout.

issues.user_problem: Users misjudge checkout length
signals_to_detect: Progress bar shows more steps completed than actual checkout stages remaining (e.g., shows 75% when 50% done)
Progress indicator labels don't match actual checkout stages user must complete
Hidden steps appear after progress shows 80%+ completion (surprise additional steps)
Progress bar jumps backward or updates inconsistently as user progresses through checkout
issues.recommendation: Align progress bar with real steps
acceptance_criteria: Progress steps match actual flow
negative_signals: Progress indicator shows all actual steps (if 5 steps, shows 5 segments)
Step labels match actual checkout stages user will complete
Progress bar fills accurately as user completes each stage
No hidden steps appear after progress shows 100%
issues.context_notes: Requires testing complete checkout flow to verify accuracy. Only flag if: (1) Progress indicator demonstrably inaccurate (shows wrong % complete), OR (2) Step labels mislabel stages, OR (3) Hidden steps appear unexpectedly. Do not flag: Single-page checkouts with section indicators, or minor labeling differences. Cannot be verified from single screenshot.

refinement_v3_4.sehaa_finding: Flagged when condition not fully met

issues.user_problem: Users abandon due to missing options
signals_to_detect: Only credit card option available (no digital wallets, COD, or alternative payments)
Payment method selection limited to single provider (Stripe only, or single card type)
No Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, or regional payment methods visible
Checkout flow does not offer installment plans or BNPL options where available
issues.recommendation: Add Apple Pay, COD, wallets
acceptance_criteria: Multiple payment methods available
negative_signals: At least 3 payment methods available (card, digital wallet, COD)
Popular local payment options included (e.g., Tabby, PayPal)
Payment icons visible before checkout to set expectations
Guest checkout allows multiple payment types

issues.user_problem: Users can't identify primary actions
signals_to_detect: Shop Now button uses different color or style across different pages (Homepage vs PLP vs PDP)
Primary CTAs (Add to Cart) mix button styles (outline, solid, ghost) across pages
Same action has different button text or visual treatment on different pages
CTAs within same page use conflicting colors, sizes, or typography weight
issues.recommendation: Define and enforce CTA styles
acceptance_criteria: Primary CTA consistent across site
negative_signals: Primary CTA uses solid color, secondary actions use outline or ghost style
All primary CTAs use consistent color throughout site
Button hierarchy clear through size and color differentiation
Destructive actions use different color from primary
issues.context_notes: Only flag if CTA styling is genuinely inconsistent AND confusing. Do not flag: Intentional variations for different action types (destructive vs. primary). Focus on: Whether user can identify what's clickable and primary action.

issues.user_problem: Low-vision users struggle to read
signals_to_detect: Body text or product descriptions use light gray text on white or light background
Secondary text or labels appear in very light gray without sufficient contrast to background
Product pricing or discount information difficult to read due to color contrast
Navigation links or interactive elements use low-contrast colors (light on light)
issues.recommendation: Ensure WCAG AA contrast
acceptance_criteria: Text meets WCAG AA contrast
negative_signals: Body text meets WCAG AA contrast ratio (4.5:1 minimum)
All text readable without zooming or straining
Light gray text reserved only for truly optional secondary content
Important information (price, availability) uses high-contrast colors

issues.user_problem: Error messages use technical jargon or unclear language
signals_to_detect: Error messages use technical terms (Invalid SSL cert, 403 Forbidden, Malformed request)
Form validation errors do not specify what was wrong or how to fix it
Error text is vague (Error occurred, Try again later) without explanation
Multiple error messages appear without guidance on which field to correct first
issues.recommendation: Use plain language error messages that clearly state what went wrong
acceptance_criteria: Errors explain cause and recovery
negative_signals: Error messages use plain language explaining what's wrong
Messages explain what went wrong and how to fix it
No technical codes or jargon visible to users
Error messages are contextual to the specific field or action
issues.context_notes: Only flag truly unclear error messages. Do not flag: Technical but understandable terms for technical audience. Industry context: Developer tools may use technical errors appropriately. Focus on: Whether target audience understands message.

issues.user_problem: Users receive generic content despite sharing preferences
signals_to_detect: Homepage or product recommendations appear identical for all users (no user-specific content)
Browse history, saved items, or wishlist not used to customize recommendations
Search results or category pages show same products regardless of user segment
No personalized messaging (Hello {name}, Your recent items, etc.) throughout site
issues.recommendation: Use user preferences to personalize content and journeys
acceptance_criteria: Personalized content appears based on user interests
negative_signals: Homepage shows personalized recommendations based on browsing history
Returning users see 'Welcome back' with recently viewed items
Product suggestions based on previous purchases or viewed categories
User preferences (language, currency) remembered across sessions

issues.user_problem: App does not proactively help users during journeys
signals_to_detect: No contextual help, tooltips, or onboarding prompts visible during key tasks
Absence of cart abandonment reminders, discount alerts, or time-sensitive offers
No helpful suggestions (Did you know?, Tips, Try searching for) on empty states or slow pages
Product pages lack suggestions for next steps or related items to explore
issues.recommendation: Add reminders, notifications, contextual tips
acceptance_criteria: Users receive timely guidance without manual search
negative_signals: System suggests next steps contextually
Helpful tips appear at right moment
Proactive error prevention shown
Smart defaults based on previous behavior

issues.user_problem: Users struggle to find content quickly
signals_to_detect: No search bar, search icon, or search field visible in header on Homepage
Search missing from header on Product Listing Pages (category/collection pages)
Search missing from header on Product Detail Pages
Search functionality accessible only through footer links or hidden menu (not in main header)
issues.recommendation: Add persistent global search
acceptance_criteria: Search available from all main screens
negative_signals: Search bar prominently placed in header across Homepage, PLP, and PDP
Search icon visible in mobile header (collapsible or icon-only is acceptable)
Search accessible via one click from all major pages
Absence from checkout or cart overlay is acceptable (focused conversion flows)
issues.context_notes: Search must be missing from at least 2 of: Homepage, PLP, PDP, or Category pages. Absence from checkout/payment flows is expected.

issues.user_problem: Users receive errors but no clear path or instructions to fix them
signals_to_detect: Error message text does not specify what was wrong or how to fix (e.g., 'Invalid input')
No indication of which form field contains error or needs correction
Help text or examples absent when form field error occurs
No link to support, FAQ, or undo action after error state
issues.recommendation: Provide actionable recovery steps with each error (e.g., "Try again" or "Contact support")
acceptance_criteria: Errors clearly explain cause and fix
negative_signals: Error messages include 'How to fix' instructions
Links to help articles or support provided with errors
Contact information shown when errors can't be self-resolved
Retry or alternative action buttons included
issues.context_notes: Only flag if error provides no path forward. Do not flag: Clear error with obvious fix even without explicit instructions. Focus on: Whether user knows what to do next. Common false positive: Flagging messages that are clear from context.

issues.user_problem: Users lose context when scrolling
signals_to_detect: Header/navigation menu disappears when user scrolls down the page
Logo not visible after scrolling below initial viewport
Shopping cart or account icon not accessible while scrolling content
No sticky breadcrumb trail or context indicator visible during scroll
issues.recommendation: Make headers sticky on scroll
acceptance_criteria: Header remains visible on scroll
negative_signals: Header with navigation and cart remains visible during scroll
Product title and price stick to top on PDP when scrolling
Filter sidebar header remains visible during long filter lists
Key information accessible without scrolling back up
issues.context_notes: Only flag for long-scrolling pages where losing context hinders task completion. Do not flag: Short pages, sticky headers with limited info, pages where scrolling up is natural. Context: PDP with long descriptions benefits more than short homepage. Mobile vs desktop may differ.

issues.user_problem: Interactive elements under 44x44px cause tap errors on mobile
signals_to_detect: Links or buttons appear significantly smaller than 44px square on mobile viewport
Navigation menu items closely spaced with insufficient padding
Add-to-cart or checkout buttons appear cramped without adequate spacing
Icon-only buttons without visible text label or adequate button size
issues.recommendation: Increase touch target to 44px
acceptance_criteria: All tappable elements meet size guidelines
negative_signals: All interactive elements minimum 44x44px on mobile
Adequate spacing between touch targets (8px+ gap)
Icon buttons have sufficient padding around the icon
Clickable areas extend beyond visible button edges
issues.context_notes: All interactive elements should be minimum 44x44px on mobile viewports. Do not flag: Desktop-only interfaces, elements that expand on tap, or when adequate spacing prevents mis-taps. Only flag when: Mobile users would genuinely struggle to tap accurately. Test on actual mobile devices/viewports below 768px.

issues.issue_title: Weak value proposition above the fold
issues.user_problem: Users cannot quickly understand what the site offers
signals_to_detect: Hero section heading is vague (Welcome, Best Selection, Shop Now) without clear site mission
No supporting subheading or description explaining what products/services are offered
Value proposition buried below large visuals or placed lower on page
Unclear if site is for shoes, electronics, furniture, etc. from initial view
issues.recommendation: Clarify value proposition with concise headline and subtext
acceptance_criteria: Primary value proposition visible without scrolling
negative_signals: Videos include captions or transcripts
Audio content has text alternative available
Video player has accessible controls with keyboard navigation
Captions can be toggled on/off by user

issues.user_problem: Large visuals delay task completion
signals_to_detect: Hero image takes up more than 50% of initial viewport height
Primary CTA button difficult to spot amid large hero graphic
Users must scroll significantly to see main navigation or product categories
Hero section provides no clear entry point to primary user task (search, browse, etc.)
issues.recommendation: Reduce hero size or add clear task CTA
acceptance_criteria: Users can identify primary task immediately
negative_signals: Hero section occupies less than 40% of viewport height
Primary CTA clearly visible above fold without scrolling
Hero provides immediate access to main shopping task (search, browse, featured products)
Hero content is relevant product photography, not generic lifestyle imagery
issues.context_notes: Only flag if hero occupies >50% of initial viewport AND pushes primary shopping task below fold. Do not flag if: Hero is large but includes product showcase or clear shopping entry point. Industry context: Lifestyle/brand-focused sites may intentionally use large heroes; flag only when it hinders task completion.

issues.user_problem: Icons mean different things across pages
signals_to_detect: Cart icon used differently on Homepage vs PDP (different style, color, or placement)
Search icon represented differently across navigation and header
Star/heart icon for favorites shown in different style on different pages
Menu icon burger/hamburger design changes between layouts
issues.recommendation: Standardize icon usage and meaning
acceptance_criteria: Icons behave consistently site-wide
negative_signals: Same icon represents same function sitewide
Icon style consistent (all outlined or all filled)
Icon meanings follow common conventions
Icon + text label used consistently for clarity

issues.user_problem: Too many menu items overwhelm users
signals_to_detect: Main navigation contains 10+ top-level items without clear grouping or hierarchy
Navigation menu items compete for attention without clear visual organization
No differentiation between primary categories and secondary utility links in navigation
Navigation requires horizontal scrolling or wrapping to show all items
issues.recommendation: Group navigation items and reduce top-level options
acceptance_criteria: Navigation limited to manageable categories
negative_signals: Main navigation has 5-7 top-level items maximum
Categories logically grouped with clear labels
Mega menu organizes subcategories with visual hierarchy
Less important links moved to footer or utility navigation
issues.context_notes: Only flag if navigation has 10+ top-level items AND lacks clear organization. Standard 7-9 item navigation is acceptable if well-organized. Do not flag: Mega menus with good categorization, or navigation with clear primary/secondary distinction. Industry context: Large marketplaces may legitimately have more categories. Focus on: Whether navigation is overwhelming, not just number of items.

refinement_v3_4.sehaa_finding: Flagged when condition not fully met

issues.user_problem: Users don't know where they are
signals_to_detect: Current page menu item not visually distinguished from other navigation items
No color, underline, bold, or highlight indicating which page user is on
Breadcrumb trail absent or not highlighting current location
Page title does not match active navigation item language/style
issues.recommendation: Add clear active state styling
acceptance_criteria: Active page clearly highlighted
negative_signals: Clear visual hierarchy with distinct heading sizes
Important content uses larger fonts and bolder weights
Related content visually grouped with whitespace
Call-to-action elements stand out through size and color

issues.user_problem: Users cannot judge result usefulness
signals_to_detect: Search results page shows products without images or key product information
Results list lacks category labels, ratings, or prices to help differentiate items
No visual grouping or sort order clues (relevance score, popularity badges) visible
Result snippets too brief to evaluate match quality
issues.recommendation: Add thumbnails, categories, or highlights
acceptance_criteria: Results clearly differentiated
negative_signals: Search results show product images, price, and key specs
Results include category tags or filters applied
Relevance indicators like 'Best Match' shown
Search term highlighted in results
issues.context_notes: Only flag if search results genuinely lack helpful information. Do not flag: Minimal but sufficient info (image + price + title is often adequate). Industry context: Marketplace sites need more detail than single-brand stores. Focus on: Whether user can evaluate results.

issues.user_problem: Users can’t control product order
signals_to_detect: Product listing page displays no sort options dropdown or buttons
Sort controls hidden in secondary menu instead of prominently displayed with results
Only basic sort available (oldest to newest) without common options (price, relevance, popularity)
No ability to reverse sort order (ascending/descending)
acceptance_criteria: Users can easily reorder results
negative_signals: Sort dropdown offers at least 3 relevant options (Price, Popularity, Newest)
Sort controls prominently displayed above product grid
Sort includes both ascending and descending for price/date
Default sort option clearly indicated
issues.context_notes: Single-category pages with <10 products may not need sorting. B2B sites may prioritize different sorts than B2C. Medical/regulated products may limit sort by price for compliance reasons. Only flag when: PLP has 15+ products AND sort completely absent AND would benefit user decision-making.

issues.user_problem: Users lose applied filters
signals_to_detect: Applied filters (e.g., color=red, price=0-50) disappear after navigating to related page
Filter state not preserved in URL or via page back navigation
User must re-apply filters after clicking individual product or pagination
No indicator or reminder showing filters are active when returning to listings
acceptance_criteria: Filters remain applied until cleared
negative_signals: Applied filters persist when navigating to product and back
Filter state maintained in URL parameters
Browser back button restores previous filter selections
Badge shows active filters when returning to PLP
issues.context_notes: Only flag if filters reset unexpectedly during same session. Do not flag: Filter reset between different sessions (acceptable), or when navigating to unrelated category. Common false positive: Browser back button behavior that's actually browser-standard.

issues.user_problem: Users don’t understand filter meaning
signals_to_detect: Filter labels use jargon or abbreviations (SKU, GTIN, Material Code) instead of common terms
Filter options unclear (e.g., 'Fit Type: A, B, C' without explanation what A/B/C mean)
Filter categories not organized logically (Price before Size, Color below Weight, etc.)
No help text or examples showing what filtering by each option does
acceptance_criteria: Filters are self-explanatory
negative_signals: Filter labels use common terms not codes
Filter options clearly describe what they do
Help tooltips available for complex filters
Filter categories organized in logical order
issues.context_notes: Only flag if filter labels are genuinely unclear (codes, abbreviations, jargon). Do not flag: Industry-standard terms (e.g., 'Bluetooth 5.0' for electronics is clear to target audience). Industry context: Technical products may use technical terms appropriately.

issues.user_problem: Users can’t inspect product properly
signals_to_detect: Product images appear small or pixelated on PDP
Single static image shown without thumbnail gallery or additional views
No zoom functionality available (click to enlarge, magnifying glass, etc.)
Images from different angles or details not provided for product inspection
acceptance_criteria: Users can clearly inspect product
negative_signals: Product images clickable to open large view or zoom
Zoom functionality available on hover or click
Multiple images at high resolution provided
360-degree view or video available for complex products
issues.context_notes: Only flag if no way to view product detail (no zoom, single small image, no enlargement). Do not flag: High-res images even without explicit zoom. Industry context: Digital products may not need zoom; physical products typically do.

issues.user_problem: Users don’t see social proof
signals_to_detect: Product reviews or ratings not visible until scrolling below price/add-to-cart section
Review section buried in tabs or collapsed sections instead of prominently displayed
Star rating or review count not shown near product title or price
No aggregated reviews summary (e.g., '4.5 stars from 256 reviews') visible above fold
acceptance_criteria: Reviews visible early on PDP
negative_signals: Reviews section visible on PDP without scrolling far
Star rating displayed prominently near product title
Review count clickable to jump to reviews
Review summary shown above fold

issues.user_problem: Users unsure if item is available
signals_to_detect: Product cards on PLP lack any stock status indicator (no 'In Stock', 'Out of Stock', 'Low Stock' badges)
Stock information inconsistent (some products show status, others don't for no clear reason)
Out-of-stock items displayed without clear unavailability indication or disabled add-to-cart
PDP shows no stock status before user attempts to add to cart
acceptance_criteria: Availability shown before add-to-cart
negative_signals: All product cards consistently show stock status (In Stock, Out of Stock, Low Stock)
Stock availability visible without hovering or clicking
Out-of-stock items clearly marked with Add to Cart disabled
Stock status uses consistent color coding (green=available, red=unavailable)
issues.context_notes: Must test multiple scenarios: (1) In-stock products, (2) Out-of-stock products, (3) Low-stock products. Only flag if: Inconsistent display (some show, some don't) OR out-of-stock items not clearly marked OR completely missing from all products. Do not flag: Consistent 'In Stock' on all available items if out-of-stock products are removed from display or clearly marked. Industry context: Some luxury brands intentionally hide stock levels.

refinement_v3_4.sehaa_finding: Flagged when condition not fully met

issues.user_problem: Users surprised by final cost
signals_to_detect: Product price displayed without showing tax, duty, or shipping fees on PDP
Final cost only revealed at checkout, not in cart summary
No breakdown showing base price vs. taxes vs. shipping before purchase
Discount or promotion applied but final savings amount not clearly calculated
acceptance_criteria: Total cost expectations set early
negative_signals: Price breakdown shows subtotal, tax, shipping before checkout
Final price with all fees visible on cart page
Each line item shows individual price and quantity
Currency and VAT/tax inclusion clearly stated

issues.user_problem: Users don’t know how to update cart
signals_to_detect: Edit quantity or remove buttons for cart items not visible or clearly labeled
Quantity field not easily editable (requires right-click menu, special click, etc.)
Remove/delete option hidden in submenu or requires multiple steps
Cart line items appear uneditable or static without clear affordance
acceptance_criteria: Users can easily edit cart
negative_signals: Edit quantity with clearly visible +/- buttons or input field
Remove button visible on each cart item
Edit options accessible without re-adding product
Save for later option available
issues.context_notes: Only flag if edit/remove actions are genuinely hidden or unclear. Do not flag: Standard patterns (trash icon, +/- buttons) even if not labeled. Focus on: Whether average user can modify cart without help.

issues.user_problem: Users abandon due to surprises
signals_to_detect: Cart page shows subtotal but no shipping cost estimate above checkout button
Shipping cost only calculated after entering address at checkout
No visible shipping cost in cart summary or order total
Free shipping threshold not indicated if applicable (e.g., 'Free shipping on orders over $50')
acceptance_criteria: Shipping costs visible before checkout
negative_signals: Shipping cost calculated and shown on cart or early in checkout
Shipping calculator available with postal code input
Free shipping threshold clearly displayed
Shipping costs visible before payment information
issues.context_notes: Only flag if shipping cost hidden until final checkout step. Do not flag if: Cost shown on cart page, shipping calculator available, or free shipping clearly stated. Industry context: Some regions require checkout for accurate shipping; flag based on when user learns cost relative to commitment level.

issues.user_problem: Users forced to create accounts
signals_to_detect: Checkout page requires account creation before proceeding with order
No prominent Guest Checkout or Continue as Guest option visible
Guest option buried deep in checkout flow rather than offered upfront
Account creation mandatory with no skip or bypass available
acceptance_criteria: Guest checkout clearly offered
negative_signals: Guest checkout prominently offered as primary option
'Continue as Guest' button equal or larger than account login
Guest checkout doesn't require account creation
Account creation offered after purchase, not forced
issues.context_notes: Only flag if account creation is REQUIRED to complete purchase. Do not flag if: Guest checkout available even if account login is prominent. Industry context: B2B or regulated products (alcohol, pharma) may legitimately require accounts; flag based on industry norms.

issues.user_problem: Users struggle to complete checkout
signals_to_detect: Checkout form displays billing and shipping fields randomly mingled (address line 1, city, billing address, zip, shipping address line 2)
No visual grouping or section headers separating billing, shipping, payment information
Fields not organized in typical flow order (shipping address, billing address, payment)
Form lacks spacing or dividers making sections unclear
acceptance_criteria: Forms visually segmented
negative_signals: Form fields grouped logically
Related fields visually grouped with borders or spacing
Clear section headings separate different form areas
Logical tab order follows visual grouping

issues.user_problem: Users discover errors too late
signals_to_detect: Form field errors only shown when user submits entire form, not during entry
No real-time feedback as user types (e.g., email field doesn't check format until blur/submit)
Required fields not marked until user attempts submission
No character count or validation hints as user fills field
acceptance_criteria: Errors shown as user types
issues.context_notes: Cannot verify from static screenshots. Requires: (1) Video of form interaction, (2) Testing email/phone validation, (3) Observing error timing.
negative_signals: Form fields show validation as user types or on blur
Checkmarks appear when field correctly filled
Error messages appear immediately when user leaves invalid field
Password strength indicator updates in real-time

issues.issue_title: Primary CTA below the fold on page load
issues.user_problem: Main conversion button not visible without scrolling down initially
signals_to_detect: Complete Checkout or Place Order button located far down page requiring scroll after loading
Primary CTA button not visible in initial viewport on checkout page
Pay Now or Submit Order button positioned below fold on mobile
CTA obscured by sticky elements or overlaid content
acceptance_criteria: CTA always visible
negative_signals: Primary CTA visible in initial viewport without scrolling
Add-to-cart or checkout button appears above fold
Mobile layout ensures CTA visible in first screen
Sticky CTA appears if main button scrolls out
issues.context_notes: Only flag if: Primary CTA not visible on initial page load AND no sticky CTA appears when scrolling. Do not flag: Mobile layouts where some scroll expected, or if CTA becomes sticky when main scrolls out. Context: 'Above fold' varies by device; focus on accessibility within first screen.

issues.user_problem: Users doubt payment safety
signals_to_detect: Checkout page lacks trust badges, security icons, or SSL certificate indicators
No reassuring text about payment security (e.g., Your payment is secure, Encrypted, PCI compliant)
Payment section does not display security logos (Visa, Mastercard, Stripe, etc.)
No privacy policy disclosure or data protection statement near payment form
acceptance_criteria: Security reassurance visible
negative_signals: Security badges visible on checkout

issues.user_problem: Users unsure system is responding

negative_signals: Spinner or loading animation appears during async operations

Progress indicator for multi-step operations

issues.user_problem: Users don't understand terminology

negative_signals: Same concept uses same term throughout site

Action verbs consistent
Terminology guide followed

issues.issue_title: Weak error recovery and dead-end handling

negative_signals: Errors include actionable next steps or retry buttons
Alternative options offered when primary path fails
Contact support easily accessible from error states
Clear path back to working state provided
issues.context_notes: Only flag genuine dead-ends (error with no recovery path). Do not flag: Errors with back button, contact option, or obvious recovery. Focus on: Whether user has ANY way forward from error state.

issues.issue_title: Insufficient system feedback during multi-step actions

negative_signals: Loading states, confirmations, and processing feedback provided
User knows system is working
Multi-step actions show which step is in progress
Completion confirmation appears after action finishes

issues.issue_title: Poor expectation setting before irreversible actions
issues.user_problem: Users commit to an action without understanding prerequisites, constraints, or consequences, leading to surprise and frustration.
nielsen_heuristic: Match between system and the real world
signals_to_detect: Booking or purchase button lacks clear terms or cancellation policy link

negative_signals: Actions with consequences show preview or confirmation
Irreversible actions require explicit confirmation
Prerequisites clearly stated before action button
Warning messages explain what will happen
issues.context_notes: Only flag irreversible actions without ANY confirmation. Do not flag: Delete with undo option, or consequence is obvious. Industry context: Bulk actions, payments, deletions should require confirmation. Focus on: Risk level of action.

issues.issue_title: Mismatch between explanatory content and interaction behavior

FAQ describes process different from actual implementation in UI
issues.recommendation: Align explanatory content with real interaction behavior and edge cases.
acceptance_criteria: Guidance text matches the actual flow and outcomes users experience.
negative_signals: Help text accurately describes what happens
FAQs match actual system behavior
Tooltips provide accurate information
Examples reflect current UI

issues.issue_title: Weak post-action reassurance and next-step clarity

signals_to_detect: Confirmation page lacks order number or clear confirmation message

Confirmation missing guidance on when product will arrive or booking confirmed
issues.recommendation: Provide clear confirmation plus next steps (what’s done, what’s next, where to track).
acceptance_criteria: After completion, users see an explicit confirmation and clear next step guidance (e.g., track order, view booking).
negative_signals: Success confirmation message appears after action
Next steps clearly indicated
Clear path to continue journey
Confirmation includes summary of what was accomplished

issues.issue_title: Disabled search button forcing keyboard entry

signals_to_detect: Search button appears disabled or grayed out until text is entered

negative_signals: Search button functional and clickable at all times
Both button click and Enter key submit search
Search icon button has clear hover/focus state
Empty search handled gracefully
issues.context_notes: Only flag if search button completely non-functional. Do not flag: Search that works via Enter key, or button that triggers on input focus. Common false positive: Styling that looks disabled but button actually works.

issues.issue_title: No spelling suggestions or error handling in search
issues.user_problem: Users receive no feedback when search terms are misspelled
signals_to_detect: No zero results message or suggestion when query returns no matches
Search missing Did you mean or autocorrect for misspelled terms

issues.recommendation: Implement fuzzy search and provide "Did you mean" suggestions for misspelled queries
acceptance_criteria: System suggests corrections for misspelled search terms
negative_signals: 'Did you mean' suggestions appear for misspelled searches
Zero results page offers corrected spelling alternatives
Similar search terms suggested
Related categories shown on no results
issues.context_notes: Only flag zero-results pages with no helpful alternatives. Do not flag: Sites with small catalogs where misspelling suggestions aren't feasible. Focus on: Whether user has path forward after no results.

issues.issue_title: Search bar occupies excessive screen space
issues.user_problem: Search element takes up too much real estate, cluttering navigation
signals_to_detect: Search input field takes up more than 50% of header or navigation bar width
Search bar doesn't collapse or resize on mobile viewports below 480px

negative_signals: Search bar proportionate to header space
Search collapses to icon on mobile
Search size balanced with other header elements
Compact search design doesn't dominate
issues.context_notes: Only flag if search genuinely dominates header (>50% width) and crowds out other elements. Do not flag: Prominent but proportionate search, or search that's primary site function. Industry context: Search-heavy sites (marketplaces) may legitimately emphasize search.

issues.issue_title: Limited filter categories without count previews
issues.user_problem: Users cannot see how many results each filter option will return
signals_to_detect: Filter options lack count in parentheses showing matching results

issues.recommendation: Show result counts next to each filter option before selection
acceptance_criteria: Each filter displays number of matching results in parentheses
negative_signals: Filter options show result counts in parentheses (e.g., 'Blue (24)')
Price filter displays min-max range of available products
Disabled filter options indicate no results or are hidden
Filter counts update dynamically as filters are applied
issues.context_notes: Only flag if filter counts completely absent AND would help user decision. Do not flag: Small catalogs (<50 products), filters where counts don't add value (color options), or when counts load progressively. Focus on: User benefit of count information.

issues.user_problem: Sort options like 'lowest rating' may reduce trust and conversion
signals_to_detect: Sort dropdown offers Lowest Rating or Worst Reviewed option

issues.recommendation: Remove or reconsider sort options that highlight negative aspects

negative_signals: Sort options focus on positive attributes
Negative sort options clearly labeled if present
Default sort is quality-focused
Options prioritize customer benefit
issues.context_notes: Only flag if negative sort options are default or prominently featured. Do not flag: Presence of 'Low to High' price sort (this is useful). Flag: 'Lowest Rated', 'Most Returns', 'Worst Reviewed' sorts that highlight poor products. Context: Academic/research sites may legitimately need all sort options.

issues.issue_title: Cannot deselect filter options once selected

Each active filter has individual remove option
issues.context_notes: Only flag if filters are one-way (can apply but cannot remove individually). Do not flag: Radio buttons (one selection by design), or if 'Clear All' is acceptable pattern for simple filters. Focus on: Whether user can modify selections without starting over.

Screen readers can interpret filters
issues.context_notes: Only flag icon-only filters that are genuinely ambiguous. Do not flag: Universal icons (star for rating, $ for price) or when tooltips clarify. Industry context: Fashion sites may use color swatches (acceptable), technical sites need text labels.

issues.issue_title: Missing country code prefix for phone input

issues.context_notes: Only flag if breadcrumbs and navigation are genuinely confusing (same styling, position). Do not flag: Similar-ish styling if clear contextually. Focus on: Whether user can distinguish navigation from location trail.

issues.issue_title: Non-responsive dropdown menu on different screen sizes

issues.user_problem: Users cannot change site language despite selector being present
